summary: Persistent pinned-session divergence after asynchronous prewarm causes repeated fallback loop
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated requests routed to a legacy model variant despite an explicit tenant pin to a new canary variant. Traffic exhibits a repeated fallback loop: request -> pinned variant mismatch -> orchestrator fallback -> edge retry selecting legacy variant -> client reports mixed outputs.

Impact: Multiple production endpoints for Lumina Health are returning inconsistent model outputs for the same session (affecting user-facing clinical summarization). Observed token-level quality regressions and a billing spike due to duplicated attempts. Estimated 12% of requests for the tenant in us-east experienced diverged model responses over the last 2 hours.

Environment: Dedicated pool for Lumina Health in prod (us-east). Canary rollout started at 2026-03-12T22:00Z with a progressive weight increase and asynchronous prewarm of the canary instances (prewarm completed at varying times across nodes).

Observed behaviour: 1) Tenant pinned via API to model redwood/open-7b-v2. 2) Edge cookie and orchestrator affinity appear to favor legacy variant redwood/decoder-compat-legacy-6b after orchestrator fallback. 3) Pin state in control plane indicates tenant pinned, but edge-layer routing uses stale cohort fingerprint for a subset of requests, reintroducing legacy variant. 4) When fallback happens, orchestrator issues a retry that sometimes arrives back at edge with older routing metadata causing another fallback -> loop.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use tenant with pinned model: call PUT /v1/tenants/<tenant>/pin {model: 'redwood/open-7b-v2'}
2) Trigger progressive canary rollout (weight ramp 1% -> 50% over 30 minutes) with asynchronous prewarm enabled for canary nodes
3) Generate session traffic with persistent session cookie; observe decisions at the edge and orchestrator traces
4) Inspect requests that receive model outputs from redwood/decoder-compat-legacy-6b and follow header X-RW-Route-ID and X-RW-Pin-Fingerprint across hops
5) Repeat during a small burst (traffic surge) to reveal retry/fallback loop behavior
logs_snippets: [2026-03-13T00:14:02Z] edge-01 TRACE tenant=lumina session=abc123 RouteFingerprint=0x7f4 fallback_reason=variant_unavailable -> ORCH_RETRY
[2026-03-13T00:14:02Z] edge-01 INFO tenant=lumina incoming_retry session=abc123 RouteFingerprint=0x7f4 resolved_variant=redwood/decoder-compat-legacy-6b note=pin_state=confirmed
[2026-03-13T00:14:03Z] svc-prewarm-03 INFO canary_prewarm_complete node=canary-03 latency_smooth=0.08s prewarm_finish=2026-03-13T00:12:58Z
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: customer shows consistent API-level pin; edge returns inconsistent variants for ~1 in 8 requests.

SRE attached distributed traces from edge -> orchestrator -> runtime. Observed that RouteFingerprint used by edge for cohort routing was stale on some edge nodes immediately after canary prewarm finishes.

Hypothesis 1: Asynchronous prewarm completes after canary weight change; some edge nodes update routing metadata earlier/later producing mismatch between edge fingerprint and orchestrator's pin mapping.

Hypothesis 2: Retry path sets a reduced metadata set (missing X-RW-Pin-Fingerprint) causing orchestrator to fall back to a default variant; the retry then returns to the edge which still believes tenant is pinned, creating oscillation.
Checked config: TTLs for route fingerprint caching: edge-cache-ttl=30s, control-plane-snapshot-apply=5s — found a window where edge-cached fingerprint could be older than new snapshot.
Found evidence of header sanitizer sidecar rewriting cookie Domain/Path on retries (see edge logs) which can break cohort cookie matching and unstick session affinity.
SRE reproduced locally by simulating staggered prewarm finishing times across 10 edge nodes; reproduced a 10-15% divergence rate when prewarm finishing was non-uniform and retry enabled.
root_cause: Race between asynchronous canary prewarm completion and progressive weight change combined with edge route-fingerprint cache TTL + missing pin fingerprint on orchestrator retry. Sidecar header sanitizer mutated retry cookies, breaking cohort affinity and causing orchestrator to select legacy variant on fallback leading to repeated loop.
mitigation_taken: Immediate: Disabled automatic retry path for pinned tenant lumina until routing metadata reconciliation completed (edge config override applied at 2026-03-13T01:10Z).
Applied temporary edge-cache-ttl reduction to 5s for affected edge shard to reduce stale fingerprint window.
Coordination: Asked client to pause traffic surge and routing to avoid further fallback churn; Lumina applied temporary rate-limit until mid-rollout.
Added temporary policy to preserve X-RW-Pin-Fingerprint on orchestrator retry path (hotfix PR created: see related_github_prs)
next_steps: 1) Deploy orchestrator hotfix to always forward pin fingerprint on retry (PR #2891 staged to canary on 2026-03-14).
2) Implement deterministic prewarm completion handshake so snapshot apply and edge fingerprint bump are coordinated (design doc link to be added to confluence runbook).
3) Reconcile cookie sanitizer behavior: prevent mutation of pin/cohort cookie during retries; add integration test.
4) Postmortem: capture timeline, add alert on >5% tenant-diverged-responses over 10 minutes during canary windows.
5) Follow-up with Lumina Health CS: confirm client didn't observe persistent data leakage and issue customer-facing summary and credits if billing impact confirmed.
resolution_notes: Work in progress: temporary mitigations applied and orchestrator fingerprint-preservation hotfix under canary testing. Once hotfix is verified we will re-run a controlled canary for Lumina with synchronous prewarm handshake and monitor for divergence for 2 hours. Plan to issue a detailed postmortem and any credits if billing overage attributable to retries is confirmed.
